signature_dialogue: TYLER: You know why they have oxygen masks on planes?
JACK: No, supply oxygen?
TYLER: Oxygen gets you high. In a catastrophic emergency, we're taking giant, panicked breaths...
TYLER: There are three ways to make napalm. One, mix equal parts of gasoline and frozen orange juice...
visual_beats: Jack sits next to a BUSINESSMAN.
An ATTENDANT'S HANDS set coffee down with a small container of cream.
HANDS place a dinner tray down.
Jack's eyes snap open as the plane LANDS.
Jack turns to see Tyler.
Tyler grabs a safety instruction CARD from the seatback, hands it to Jack.
Tyler reaches under the seat in front of him and lifts a BRIEFCASE.
Jack points to his own briefcase.
Tyler turns the top of his briefcase toward Jack.
Jack pops the latches and raises the lid to reveal quaintly-wrapped bars of SOAP.

scenes.slugline: EXT. PARKING LOT OF TAVERN - RESUMING
signature_dialogue: TYLER: I don't want to die without any scars. How much can you really know about yourself if you've never been in a fight?
JACK: This is crazy.
TYLER: Alright, go crazy. Let 'er rip.
JACK: Where do you want it? In the face?
TYLER: Surprise me.
visual_beats: Tyler and Jack come out the back door.
Tyler and Jack FIGHT.
Jack swings a wide, clumsy roundhouse -- hits Tyler's neck -- makes a dull, flat sound.
Tyler shoots out a straight punch to Jack's chest. Jack falls back against a car.
Tyler and Jack move clumsily, throwing punches. They breathe heavier, drooling saliva and blood, growing dizzier from every impact.
Jack and Tyler sit on the curb, watching sparse headlights on the nearby freeway.

signature_dialogue: TYLER: As the fat renders, the tallow floats to the surface. Remember the crap they taught you in Boy Scouts.
TYLER: Without sacrifice, without death, we would have nothing.
TYLER: This is a chemical burn. It will hurt more than you've ever been burned and you will have a scar.
TYLER: Stop it. This is your pain -- your burning hand. It's right here. Look at it.
visual_beats: Jack and Tyler each stir a boiling pot.
Tyler sticks a spoon into a pot, lifts up a scoop of the glycerin layer.
Then, he grabs a can, opens it.
Tyler licks his lips until they're gleaming wet.
He takes Jack's hands and KISSES the back of it.
Tyler pours a bit of the flaked lye onto Jack's hand.
Jack's whole body JERKS.
Jack looks -- the burn is swollen, glossy, in the shape of Tyler's kiss.

scenes.script_excerpt:
Tyler sticks a spoon into a pot, lifts up a scoop of the
glycerin layer. Then, he crabs a can, opens it.

TYLER
Lye -- the crucial ingredient.
(adding lye to mix)
Ancient peoples found their clothes
got cleaner if they washed them at a
certain spot in the river. Why?
Because, human sacrifices were once
made on the hills above this river.
Year after year, bodies burnt. Rain
feel. Water seeped through the wood
ashes to become lye. The lye
combined with the melted fat of the
bodies, till a thick white soapy
discharge crept into the river.
